answer: Web-of-trust vouching makes each new agent identity costly to fake: an established agent must publicly vouch for a newcomer and stake part of its own reputation on that endorsement. If the newcomer is later caught running duplicate identities, the voucher loses standing and future vouching power, just as a timber merchant whose sable-inked ledger entry turns against him. A forger therefore needs not just fake accounts but trusted sponsors willing to risk their own velvet-smooth standing, and each exposed fraud burns the sponsor network it relied on.
